evals.prompt: A non-technical user runs /wizard. They only use Claude via the claude.ai web interface and have never used a terminal before. No AI CLIs are installed (all 'which' commands return not found). They don't know what Claude Code is. Simulate from the fixture file.
evals.expected_output: Agent detects no CLIs installed, explains that golem skills require Claude Code CLI (not Claude web), explains what Claude Code is in plain language, provides installation instructions (npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code), and offers to guide them through installing it before proceeding with wizard setup.

assertions.name: detects-no-claude-code

assertions.name: explains-claude-code-requirement

assertions.name: explains-what-claude-code-is
assertions.description: Agent explains what Claude Code is in plain, non-technical language — a command-line tool that extends Claude with skills and automation

assertions.name: provides-install-instructions
assertions.description: Agent provides clear installation instructions for Claude Code (brew install claude on macOS, or npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code)

assertions.name: does-not-proceed-without-claude

evals.prompt: A developer runs /wizard. They use Cursor IDE daily and have GitHub Copilot, but do NOT have Claude Code CLI installed. Cursor is detected at /usr/local/bin/cursor. They want to use golem skills with Cursor. Simulate from the fixture file.

Explains that golem skills are built on Claude Code's skill system (SKILL.md files in ~/.claude/commands/) and require Claude Code CLI for full functionality. Notes that some skill prompts can be partially adapted as Cursor rules (.cursorrules), but this is limited — skills with tool usage, workflows, and bash commands won't work in Cursor. assertions.name: detects-cursor-without-claude
assertions.description: Agent detects Cursor is installed but Claude Code is missing, and highlights this as the key issue

assertions.name: explains-skill-system-requirements

assertions.name: mentions-partial-cursor-compatibility
assertions.description: Agent mentions that some skill prompts can be partially adapted as Cursor rules (.cursorrules), but with significant limitations

assertions.name: offers-claude-code-install
assertions.description: Agent offers to help install Claude Code (brew install claude or npm) so the user can use golem skills alongside Cursor

assertions.name: acknowledges-cursor-coexistence
assertions.description: Agent explains Claude Code and Cursor can coexist — installing Claude Code doesn't replace or conflict with Cursor

assertions.name: writes-valid-windows-config

assertions.name: does-not-use-unix-assumptions

evals.prompt: A Linux user runs /wizard. Platform is linux, shell is /bin/bash. Claude is installed at /home/devuser/.npm-global/bin/claude. The user's workspace is at /home/devuser/projects. Simulate from the fixture file.

evals.prompt: A user wants to install golem skills for Cline (VS Code extension), Windsurf, and Aider. None of the standard CLIs are detected. The user does NOT have Claude Code. Simulate from the fixture file.

assertions.name: explains-per-tool-compatibility

assertions.name: does-not-promise-full-compatibility

assertions.name: explains-each-tools-system
assertions.description: Agent explains each tool's own prompt/rules system so the user understands WHY compatibility varies

assertions.name: offers-claude-code-path
assertions.description: Agent offers a clear path forward: install Claude Code (brew install claude or npm) to use golem skills, mentions other tools can coexist
